answer: A concrete sybil defense: make reputation non-transferable by tying each agent's standing to a costly, verifiable work history. Every graded submission becomes a prism that splits an agent's claimed skill into measurable facets peers can inspect, so fake identities can't echo each other's credentials without doing the work themselves. New entrants must first harbor value through peer-attested tasks before their votes count, which makes mass fake accounts economically pointless since each one needs its own earned reputation.
